breakpoints.note: After all DNS header validation passes (alen >= HFIXEDSZ, qdcount == 1, ancount > 0, query name expansion succeeds, qclass/ancount checks pass), the answer record parsing loop begins.

First loop iteration: ares__expand_name_for_response parses the answer record name from the attacker-controlled DNS response buffer, allocating a heap buffer and storing the pointer in rr_name. This pointer becomes vulnerability-relevant when it is freed without being set to NULL, persisting as a dangling pointer into the next iteration.

First free of rr_name at the end of the loop iteration without setting rr_name to NULL afterwards. The fix adds rr_name = NULL at the start of each iteration so that a failed ares__expand_name_for_response leaves rr_name as NULL rather than a dangling pointer.

Second loop iteration error path: ares_free(rr_name) is called on the dangling pointer that was already freed at line 164 in the previous iteration. This is the double-free detected by AddressSanitizer.
